items.title: Vince Giordano interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: Dick says, “yeah, let’s get Vince, he can bring three of his instruments and really loves playing this music too.”

ctx.x: Are you kind of, do you feel like you’re in the — at least in the circle — or you’re known for having this knowledge and this ability in this idiom so when things come up like “The Aviator” that you do get those calls?

Well yeah, in a way I’m very fortunate to be associated with this genre of music and you would think being in New York there’s not that much film work to be done and I don’t know for some reason some of the cards were in the right place for once in my life, where they chose to do these period films in New York working for Dick Hyman, who was the musical director for so many of the Woody Allen films, and Woody has a passion for the older music, and Dick says, “yeah, let’s get Vince, he can bring three of his…
